text:
alyssa: heads-up — hit a reproducible OOM on small-batch workloads on dedicated nodes this morning, p99 spikes after ~1200 requests in 5m window
alyssa: repro script attached in the gist: https://gist.github.com/foo/repro-small-batch.sh :eyes:
mike: can you paste the minimal logs? curious if it's a host staging or slab blowup
nisha: pasted logs below — looks like host staging pool filled then eviction couldn't free fast enough. relevant lines:
```
[2026-03-22T09:12:03Z] evictor: staging_pool_used=10230MB staging_pool_limit=10240MB
[2026-03-22T09:12:04Z] evictor: failed_to_offload=12 reason=quota_unavailable
[2026-03-22T09:12:05Z] allocator: transient_alloc_failed size=16MB tenant=team-x
[2026-03-22T09:12:06Z] oom-killer-sim: target_proc=runtime-worker
```
```

sam: hmm. that sequence + "failed_to_offload=12 reason=quota_unavailable" suggests the allocator path didn't fall back to host-commit because the reserve token was consumed earlier
kevin: do we have a unique path where small batches allocate many tiny KV caches that never get the high-hotness tag? could be fragmentation + tiny allocations preventing large contiguous reclaim
alyssa: repro script creates many 8-32KB allocations concurrently (micro-batching across shards) — which matches the tiny allocation pattern
mike: quick question — does the allocator return allocation metadata that indicates 'can_offload' vs 'must_host_commit'? iirc current API is just alloc(size) -> ptr, error
nisha: right now it's alloc(size) -> handle | Err. no structured hints. we do set a separate residency hint later but it's opportunistic
ops-bot: deploy: dedicated-2026-03-22T08:50 rolled with runtime v2.14.1 (evictor tweaks)
sam: proposal: add an AllocOptions bitflag field (reserve=true|false, prefer_pin=true|false) and change alloc to alloc(size, opts) -> {handle, meta_id} where meta includes frag_class, hotness_hint. then evictor can use meta for smarter leases
kevin: +1. also add a small 'atomic-reserve' call at request start so small bursts get short-term capacity, rather than failing individual allocs
alyssa: for immediate mitigation can we backport: 1) increase staging_pool_limit by 10% for Dedicated; 2) short-term change alloc path to treat tiny allocations as reclaimable (lower pin priority)
mike: agree on rollout path: emergency patch -> canary on one Dedicated pool -> monitor token/failure metrics for 2 hours -> roll
nisha: long-term RFC items: unify alloc metadata into a compact 16-byte header so we don't pay separate lookups; expose hotness buckets to admission; and add telemetry for per-alloc lifetime so we can quantify fragment-caused OOMs
sam: also we should add a unit test that simulates N tiny concurrent allocs and validates fallback to host-commit within X ms (to prevent regressions)
kevin: logging note: when we hit quota_unavailable we should include the current lease_epoch and the tenant's soft_reserve usage so triage is faster
alyssa: ack. I'll open two PRs: emergency mitigation (bump pool + lower pin priority for tiny allocs) and a follow-up RFC draft for alloc-metadata/atomic-reserve. tagging @mike @nisha for review
ops-bot: incident-tracker: created INC-2026-314 (small-batch OOM on Dedicated)
mike: thanks — if someone can tag perf/telemetry owners in the RFC that helps. also please include concrete metrics to watch (staging_pool_used, failed_to_offload, alloc_fail_rate by size bin)
alyssa: will do. good catch team :thumbsup:
